Etiquette ForAll Equestrians
1. Make sure your horse has the temperament and training for riding on con-
gested trails.
2. Advise other trail users of your horse's temperament, e.g., a horse with a
tendency to kick should always wear a red ribbon in the tail. Assume that
not everyone will know what the ribbon means; be prepared to explain or
necessary precautions to avoid trouble.
3. Obey posted speed/gait limits. Avoid cantering or galloping on busy trails.
4. Know your horse's limitations.
5. Leave gates as you find them. Obey gate closures and regulatory signs.
6. Let other trail users know when it is safe to pass you.
7. Announce your intention to pass others. Come to a walk and pass on the
left.
8. Always pick up after your horse. Keep the trailhead clear of manure and
trash. Try to keep the trail clean of manure.

Etiquette ForAll Users
01. Treat all trail users with respect and courtesy regardless of their skill
level.
02. Protect our environment. Stay on the trails. Do not cut switchbacks or
take shortcuts.
03. Stay right and pass on the left. Always look before changing on the trail.
04. Share the trail, watch and listen for others.
05. Learn and use appropriate hand signals motorized users often fail to
hear voice signals.
06. Respect trail closures; use only trails posted as open. We will be posting
signs.
07. Carry out all litter, including pet waste.
08. All users yield to horseback riders and dog teams.
09. When encountering a horse, speak in a calm, pleasant tone so it hears a
human voice. Do not hide.
10. The rider knows the Horse best. Expect the rider to advise, not as a lack
of courtesy, but rather, with knowledge of the horses temprament.
11. Dog teams cannot stop as quickly as other users. To avoid tangles and
injury to dogs, when encountering a team, stop on the side of the trail
and wait for the team to pass. Keep tight control of any pets. Obey
directions given by the musher.
12. Downhill traffic yields to uphill traffic and faster users.
13. Do not approach, scare, harass, or feed wildlife or livestock.
14. Respect private property and the privacy of people living along the trail.
15. Pets must be kept on leashes and under control.
16. Leave flowers and plants for others to enjoy. Do not pull bark from, or
otherwise damage live trees.
17. Practice no-impact trail use. Wet and muddy trails are easily damagd.
18. Travel at a safe and controlled speed. Be especially careful if ability is
limited.

Etiquette For Mountain Bikes
01. Yield right of way to all other users. Yield to uphilll users.

02. Never pass a horse from behind. Calmly ask to pass so the rider can turn
the horse around to face your bike.
